_readme: The words a card's seal panel shows a reader, in one place so the four clients cannot
drift apart on them. A client bundles this file byte-identical and pins the copy with a
test; none of them holds the prose itself.
A panel's sentence is chosen mechanically: the transition row this event matched in
act-transitions.json names a `who`, and that `who` is the key here. An opening verb has no
transition row of its own — it is the kind's `opens.verb` — and takes the `opener` key.
Rows whose `who` is `system` write no card and so ask for no sentence.
`header_format` is the panel's title with KIND replaced by the event's own act kind,
uppercased. `link_text` labels the link to the action's full history.
`verbs` is the headline word and glyph each verb's card or system line shows — the
table the four clients previously each hardcoded. A verb absent here shows itself,
`facts` are the labels an act card puts on the machine fields it understands — the
audience, money and deadline rows. The card draws one label/value row per fact in the
same key-value grid the generic card's payload rows use; names are resolved displays,
never raw DIDs. A field no entry here labels draws in the same grid under its own key,
so nothing signed is ever invisible. The note, the context link and its hash are rows of
the same grid, after the labelled facts and before any unlabelled field; pay to, payment,

sentences.opener: This opened a task with known rules: who may take it, who may work it, who may finish it. Every later step is checked against those rules before the server accepts it — an illegal step is refused and never appears here.
sentences.offeree: Only the person this task was offered to could take this step. The server checked that before accepting it — this step from anyone else is refused and never appears here.
sentences.assignee: Only the worker this task is assigned to could take this step. The server checked that before accepting it — this step from anyone else is refused and never appears here.
sentences.offerer: Only the person who posted this task could take this step. The server checked that before accepting it — this step from anyone else is refused and never appears here.
sentences.anyone: Any signed-in account could take this step, and the server checked it was legal from the task's current state before accepting it — an illegal step is refused and never appears here.
